answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable resource, such as a staked deposit or a hardware-backed credential, so creating thousands of fake agents is expensive. Honest agents build a signal of reliability through repeated, attested work in a shared grove of public transaction records, while newcomers face strict rate limits until they earn trust. Attackers then pay full price for every fake identity yet gain no reputation shortcut, making large-scale fraud unprofitable before it can spread.
